verdict.rationale: Penpot's own docs describe itself as an open-source design platform you can run in a private cloud, on-premise, or any environment you control. Official deployment paths include docker compose, a Helm Chart, OpenShift and Rancher, and several community users confirm they self-host it. Some users report crashes and lag on self-hosted instances, but that concerns stability, not whether self-hosting is offered. Missing for 10: the specific open-source license is never named, so its terms are unevidenced.

support.subject: As a developer, I can self-host the full design platform on my own infrastructure under an open-source license

citations.quote: Penpot is the only open-source design platform that is truly deployment agnostic. Run it in your private cloud, on-premise, or any environment you control.
Deploy with docker compose ... Use Kubernetes in its different flavors: Deploy the official Helm Chart, Deploy in Openshift, Deploy in Rancher
Open-source alternative with self-hosting, unlimited files, native design tokens.
Have been self-hosting this on Docker/Portainer for several weeks for a few people. Works fine so far.
